2026-08-21T03:28:48.3651434Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3652178Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3652811Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3653746Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3654471Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3655632Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3658533Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3661925Z >
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3666612Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3671380Z >
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3674191Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3676101Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3676479Z ### How to Use
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3676969Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3678227Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3679644Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3680005Z ```bash
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3681063Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3683395Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3685206Z ```
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3685638Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3686152Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3687233Z ```bash
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3688418Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3689977Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3691626Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3693093Z ```
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3693511Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3694824Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3696566Z ```bash
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3697683Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3699038Z ```
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3699452Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3700248Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3701435Z ```bash
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3702495Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3704193Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3705792Z ```
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3706203Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3706758Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3707591Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3710341Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3713711Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3714074Z ```bash
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3715155Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3716833Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3718468Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3719075Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3719946Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3721914Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3723515Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3724452Z ```
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3725038Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3726519Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3729145Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3729502Z ```bash
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3730796Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3732491Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3733889Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3734946Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3735750Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3737321Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3738422Z ```
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3738834Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3739296Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3740836Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3742728Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3744780Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3746742Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3748802Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3749840Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3750201Z ### Notes
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3750622Z 
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3751835Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3754789Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3757236Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3759665Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3761995Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3766380Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3768460Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3769821Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-21T03:28:48.3770611Z <github-context>
